notes: Fiscal year mapping: historical years use EA’s fiscal years ended near Mar 31 (FY2023 ended Apr 1, 2023; FY2024 ended Mar 30, 2024; FY2025 ended Mar 29/Mar 31, 2025). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/712515/000071251525000022/ea-20250331.htm))
EBIT proxy: EBIT in the package is operating income from the Consolidated Statements of Operations. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/712515/000071251525000022/ea-20250331.htm))

D&A definition: da uses the cash flow line “Depreciation, amortization, accretion and impairment” (GAAP). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/712515/000071251525000022/ea-20250331.htm))

NWC definition (for operating working capital): NWC = (Receivables, net + Other current assets) − (Accounts payable, accrued, and other current liabilities + Deferred net revenue (online-enabled games)), excluding cash & short-term investments and excluding current debt (senior notes current net). This produces negative NWC due to deferred revenue mechanics. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/712515/000071251525000022/ea-20250331.htm))

Tax rate: base-case tax_rate uses a normalized effective tax rate implied by EA’s disclosure that excluding the change in valuation allowance, FY2025 effective tax rate would have been 27.0%. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/712515/000071251525000022/ea-20250331.htm))

NOL balance: nol_balance set to ~3.0B net operating loss carryforwards as of Mar 31, 2025; nol_utilization_pct is a modeled assumption (0.80) due to lack of filing-level utilization schedule in this package. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/712515/000071251525000022/ea-20250331.htm))

Capital structure inputs: cash and short-term investments from the FY2025 balance sheet; debt proxied as senior notes (current net + non-current net). Lease liabilities and other financing obligations are not included because the schema only requests cash/debt-style equity bridge items. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/712515/000071251525000022/ea-20250331.htm))
Current price: pulled from the market-data tool timestamped 2026-03-21 UTC.

Comps: peer multiples sourced from ValueSense NTM peer tables; some peers show N/A or negative multiples due to forward estimate mechanics (e.g., losses/negative denominators). Treat as directional sanity checks. ([valuesense.io](https://valuesense.io/ticker/ea/ev-to-revenue-ntm))

catalysts: New franchise releases and live-service engagement that shift annual net revenue and operating income trajectories (model impacts via revenue growth and EBIT margin). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/712515/000071251525000022/ea-20250331.htm))
Potential margin inflection from cost discipline and studio investment prioritization, reflected in forward EBIT margin assumptions.
company_overview: Electronic Arts is a global developer and publisher of digital interactive entertainment, delivering games and live services across console, PC, and mobile ecosystems. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/712515/000071251525000022/ea-20250331.htm))

Revenue is supported by major franchises (notably EA SPORTS and other recurring live-service/content offerings). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/712515/000071251525000022/ea-20250331.htm))

EA’s fiscal year ends near late March (52/53-week period), which should be reflected in DCF year alignment (FY ending Mar). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/712515/000071251525000022/ea-20250331.htm))
current_context: EA released its Q3 fiscal 2026 results (quarter ended Dec 31, 2025) with business and outlook commentary as of early February 2026. ([news.ea.com](https://news.ea.com/press-releases/press-releases-details/2026/Electronic-Arts-Reports-Q3-FY26-Results/default.aspx?utm_source=openai))

Key valuation sensitivity for the model is tied to the revenue/margin path and the implied reinvestment intensity (D&A and capex as % of sales). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/712515/000071251525000022/ea-20250331.htm))
investment_highlights: Base-case thesis assumes stable reinvestment intensity (capex as % of sales) while operating margin converges toward ~21% over the forecast horizon. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/712515/000071251525000022/ea-20250331.htm))

Model captures EA’s recurring economics via negative operating NWC as a % of sales (deferred net revenue and other working-capital mechanics). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/712515/000071251525000022/ea-20250331.htm))
Terminal value framework uses Gordon growth with conservative long-run growth versus historical game-cycle volatility. (Assumption; see terminal_growth and terminal_method fields.)

Comp set focuses on interactive/gaming peers and uses NTM valuation multiples as a directional cross-check rather than a primary valuation driver. ([valuesense.io](https://valuesense.io/ticker/ea/ev-to-revenue-ntm))
key_risks: Game release timing and catalog weakness can cause downside to revenue growth relative to base-case chaining assumptions.
Margin compression risk from higher-than-modeled operating costs, including R&D and marketing, or from mix shifts across franchises.

valuation_summary: DCF input package ties historical EBIT, depreciation/amortization, and capex directly to EA’s GAAP cash flow and income statement lines from the most recent annual filings. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/712515/000071251525000022/ea-20250331.htm))
Forecast drivers are expressed consistently as margins and ratios of sales, enabling automated QA of chained revenue growth via the validation_support forecast_revenue series.

Peer multiples are presented as a sanity check only, with explicit handling of N/A or negative multiples where forward estimates imply losses or negative denominators. ([valuesense.io](https://valuesense.io/ticker/ea/ev-to-revenue-ntm))
